messages.content: You are a precise biomedical information extraction assistant. Follow the requested output format exactly and never add explanations.

You will be given a piece of text and a list of relational triples in the format of [Subject, Relation, Object] extracted from the text. For each relation present in the triples, your task is to write a description to express the meaning of the relation.

Here are some examples:
Example 1:
Text: Lipitor (atorvastatin) belongs to a group of drugs called statins. Lipitor is used together with diet to lower blood levels of "bad" cholesterol (LDL) and to reduce the risk of stroke and heart attack.
Triples: [["Lipitor", "has generic name", "atorvastatin"], ["Lipitor", "belongs to drug class", "statins"], ["Lipitor", "treats", "high LDL cholesterol"], ["Lipitor", "reduces risk of", "stroke"]]
Relations: ["has generic name", "belongs to drug class", "treats", "reduces risk of"]
Answer:
has generic name: The subject drug is known by the generic (non-proprietary) name specified by the object entity.
belongs to drug class: The subject drug is a member of the pharmacological drug class specified by the object entity.
treats: The subject drug is used to treat or manage the medical condition specified by the object entity.
reduces risk of: The subject drug is used to lower the risk of the medical event or condition specified by the object entity.

Example 2:
Text: You should not use metformin if you have severe kidney disease. Tell your doctor if you have ever had liver disease. Metformin may cause lactic acidosis, a serious condition. Avoid drinking alcohol while taking metformin.
Triples: [["metformin", "contraindicated in", "severe kidney disease"], ["metformin", "use with caution in", "liver disease"], ["metformin", "has serious side effect", "lactic acidosis"], ["metformin", "should be avoided with", "alcohol"]]
Relations: ["contraindicated in", "use with caution in", "has serious side effect", "should be avoided with"]
Answer:
contraindicated in: The subject drug should not be used by patients who have the condition specified by the object entity.
use with caution in: The subject drug may be unsafe or require medical supervision for patients who have the condition specified by the object entity.
has serious side effect: The subject drug may cause the serious or dangerous adverse effect specified by the object entity.
should be avoided with: Patients taking the subject drug should avoid the substance or activity specified by the object entity.

Example 3:
Text: Amlodipine is available as oral tablets in strengths of 2.5 mg, 5 mg, and 10 mg. Overdose symptoms may include rapid heartbeats and fainting. Norvasc is made by Pfizer.
Triples: [["amlodipine", "has dosage form", "oral tablet"], ["amlodipine", "has strength", "2.5 mg"], ["amlodipine", "has overdose symptom", "fainting"], ["Norvasc", "manufactured by", "Pfizer"]]
Relations: ["has dosage form", "has strength", "has overdose symptom", "manufactured by"]
Answer:
has dosage form: The subject drug is available in the pharmaceutical dosage form specified by the object entity.
has strength: The subject drug is available in the dose strength specified by the object entity.
has overdose symptom: An overdose of the subject drug may cause the symptom specified by the object entity.
manufactured by: The subject drug is manufactured or marketed by the company specified by the object entity.

Now please write relation descriptions given the following text and triples. Note that the description needs to be general and can be used to describe relations between other entities as well. Pay attention to the order of subject and object entities. Write exactly one line per relation in the form "relation: description" and nothing else.
Text: Cyclobenzaprine may increase the risk of seizures in people taking tramadol, and may block the blood pressure-lowering effect of guanethidine and similar drugs. 1,2,3
Tell your doctor about all your other medicines. This list is not complete, and other drugs may interact with cyclobenzaprine, including prescription and over-the-counter medicines, vitamins, and herbal products.
Can you take ibuprofen with cyclobenzaprine?:
There is no listed drug interaction between cyclobenzaprine and ibuprofen, and the two are commonly prescribed together for painful muscle injuries, since they work in different ways. In studies, taking cyclobenzaprine with aspirin did not change blood levels of either drug, and combining it with naproxen was well tolerated, although the combination caused more drowsiness than naproxen alone. Check with your doctor or pharmacist before combining medicines, especially if you take other drugs as well. 1
Can you take Tylenol with cyclobenzaprine?:
Triples: [["Cyclobenzaprine", "increases risk of", "seizures in people taking tramadol"], ["Cyclobenzaprine", "blocks blood pressure lowering effect of", "guanethidine and similar drugs"], ["Cyclobenzaprine", "interacts with", "other prescription and over-the-counter medicines"], ["Cyclobenzaprine", "interacts with", "vitamins"], ["Cyclobenzaprine", "interacts with", "herbal products"], ["Cyclobenzaprine", "has no interaction with", "ibuprofen"], ["Cyclobenzaprine", "used in combination with", "ibuprofen for painful muscle injuries"], ["Cyclobenzaprine", "has no effect on blood levels of", "aspirin"], ["Cyclobenzaprine", "combined with", "naproxen is well tolerated"], ["Cyclobenzaprine", "combined with", "naproxen causes more drowsiness than naproxen alone"], ["Cyclobenzaprine", "should be used with caution when combined with", "other drugs"], ["Cyclobenzaprine", "requires consultation with", "doctor or pharmacist before combination"]]
Relations: ["blocks blood pressure lowering effect of", "combined with", "has no effect on blood levels of", "has no interaction with", "increases risk of", "interacts with", "requires consultation with", "should be used with caution when combined with", "used in combination with"]
Answer:

completion:
blocks blood pressure lowering effect of: The subject drug inhibits or counteracts the blood pressure-lowering action of the specified drug or class of drugs.  
combined with: The subject drug is used together with the specified drug or substance, and the combination is described as well tolerated or having a specific effect.  
has no effect on blood levels of: The subject drug does not alter the plasma concentration or pharmacokinetics of the specified drug.  
has no interaction with: The subject drug does not produce a clinically significant interaction with the specified drug or substance.  
increases risk of: The subject drug may elevate the likelihood of the specified adverse event or condition occurring in individuals using the co-administered substance.  
interacts with: The subject drug may produce a clinically relevant interaction when co-administered with the specified drug, supplement, or product.  
requires consultation with: Before combining the subject drug with the specified entity, medical advice from a qualified healthcare provider is necessary.  
should be used with caution when combined with: The combination of the subject drug and the specified entity may pose a risk, and careful monitoring or medical supervision is advised.  
used in combination with: The subject drug is prescribed or administered together with the specified drug for a shared therapeutic purpose, such as treating a specific condition.
